record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Matrix Theory Arising in Linear Systems and Control
record.context_brief: robust stability certification by a test subset
record.original_question: Given a collection M of real n x n matrices, determine a subset M_0 subseteq M with the property that if every matrix in M_0 is stable, meaning that all of its eigenvalues have negative real part, then every matrix in M is stable. The source highlights this as a fundamental robust-stability problem for uncertain linear-system models and asks for such certifying subsets beyond the polynomial cases covered by Kharitonov-type results.

evidence.quote: A fundamental problem in the analysis of linear systems is the following: Given a collection of matrices M c R^{n x n}, determine a subset M_0 c M such that if every element of M_0 is stable (that is, each of its eigenvalues has negative real part), then every element of M is also stable.
This problem arises when the modeling data are uncertain and guarantees of stability are desired.

artifact.self_contained_problem: A real n×n matrix A is called (Hurwitz) stable if every eigenvalue of A has negative real part. Let M be a family (in general infinite) of real n×n matrices. A subset M_0 ⊆ M is called a stability-certifying subset for M if the following implication holds: whenever every matrix in M_0 is stable, every matrix in M is stable.\n\nProblem. Develop a general theory that, for natural classes of matrix families M ⊆ R^{n×n} (for example, families defined by interval, polytopic, affine, or other structured parametric uncertainty), identifies an explicit stability-certifying subset M_0 ⊆ M, preferably finite or of small cardinality. In particular, for classes of matrix families that go beyond those arising from interval polynomials (where Kharitonov-type results provide a four-element certifying set in coefficient space), characterize when such certifying subsets exist and how they may be constructed.
artifact.status_search_result: For matrix families this problem remains largely open. While Kharitonov-style results provide finite certifying subsets at the level of interval polynomials, and certain "edge" and "vertex" extreme-point theorems exist for restricted classes (e.g., interval polynomial matrices with structured row/column dependence), counterexamples are known showing that for general interval matrices the four "vertex" or "extreme" matrices do not suffice. No general construction of stability-certifying subsets for arbitrary matrix families is known.

status_evidence.title: A survey of extreme point results for robustness of control systems
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys extreme-point (vertex/edge) theorems showing when robust stability of a family can be verified on a finite subset.
status_evidence.claim: Extreme-point results are known only for specific classes; a general theory of certifying subsets for matrix families is not available.

status_evidence.title: A Kharitonov-like theorem for interval polynomial matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Robust stability of interval polynomial matrices reduces to checking subclasses involving Kharitonov edge and vertex polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Kharitonov-type certifying subsets exist for structured interval polynomial matrices but not in general.

status_evidence.title: Computational Complexity of Kharitonov's Robust Stability Test
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Kharitonov's finite test set for interval polynomials and complexity of robust stability tests.
status_evidence.claim: Finite certifying tests are established for polynomial coefficient uncertainty but extension to general matrix uncertainty is not.
